title: Endotherapy Application Protocol for Pest Control in Urban Trees of Bogotá D.C.
author: Gustavo Hernan Ardila Roa
materials: Preparación de la solución de agroinsumos:

steps.title: Plan Application Timing
steps.instruction: Consult Table 1 to identify the recommended lunar phase for endotherapy application for each specific tree species based on absorption time differences.

steps.title: Measure Trunk Perimeter
steps.instruction: Measure the trunk perimeter at a height of 50 cm from the base. Only trees with a perimeter greater than 50 cm are eligible to prevent the drill from reaching the heartwood.

substeps.instruction: For trees bifurcated from the base, measure the perimeter of each stem to determine the correct number of devices for the established height.

steps.title: Determine Number of Devices
steps.instruction: Calculate the number of devices required based on the trunk perimeter, using a recommended spacing of 25 to 30 cm between injection points.

substeps.instruction: Use the formula: Number of devices = round(Perimeter (cm) / 30) to the nearest integer.
Refer to Table 2 for quick estimation reference values.

steps.title: Prepare Agro-input Solution
steps.instruction: Prepare a solution with a total volume of 20 mL per device, ensuring physicochemical compatibility to avoid coagulation or phase separation.

substeps.instruction: In a clean, wide-mouth container, add water.
Incorporate the insecticide.
Add the fertilizer.
Add the resistance inducer.
Use a mixer to agitate the solution until completely homogeneous.
Refer to Table 3 for specific doses of agro-inputs.

steps.title: Fill Endotherapy Devices
steps.instruction: Fill the endotherapy devices using a 20 mL syringe.

substeps.instruction: Absorb the prepared mixture with the syringe.
Inject the full volume into the upper valve of the endotherapy device.

steps.title: Drill the Trunk
steps.instruction: Create injection holes using a 1/4 inch metal drill bit, previously disinfected with quaternary ammonium, at approximately 50 cm above ground level.

substeps.instruction: Perform the first hole at low speed to avoid cauterizing the wood.
Drill perpendicular to the trunk (90° to the stem axis).
Drill progressively in three stages: 2 cm (1/3 length), 4 cm (1/2 length), and 6 cm (full extension).
Monitor sawdust color: start with dark (bark), then light/white (xylem/target zone). Stop immediately if sawdust turns dark again, indicating heartwood has been reached.
Avoid areas with knots, cracks, protrusions, indentations, degraded sapwood, extensive necrosis, rot, structural cavities, physiological deterioration, or attached epiphytes.

steps.title: Install Connectors and Devices
steps.instruction: Install the connectors and devices following a zig-zag pattern to prevent product diffusion between holes.

substeps.instruction: Place the connector on the edge of the hole and secure it by tapping gently with a rubber mallet until fixed.
Insert the device quickly and precisely into the connector to avoid spills.
For additional devices, alternate heights at 50–60–50 cm from the base, with a horizontal distance between 25 and 37 cm.

steps.title: Monitor Absorption
steps.instruction: Observe the device until the liquid is fully absorbed by the tree's vascular system.

substeps.instruction: Confirm absorption is complete when the device is totally smooth (no longer bulging from liquid pressure).
Wait an additional 5 minutes after absorption to allow movement via transpirational flow.
Refer to Table 4 for average and maximum absorption times by species.
If a device remains full beyond the estimated time, remove and reinstall it at an alternate point on the stem where absorption was successful.

steps.title: Remove Devices and Seal Holes
steps.instruction: Remove the hardware and seal the injection site.

substeps.instruction: Remove the device from the connector.
Carefully extract the connector from the hole using pliers.
Using protective gloves, apply hormonal healing paste (e.g., Colinagro or equivalent) directly over the hole, covering all exposed tissue.
Verify no open spaces remain that could allow water or contaminants to enter.

Note: Routine sealing is not required unless there is high environmental exposure, pathogens, previous tissue damage, or tree stress; heritage trees should follow more conservative management per the Bogotá D.C. Vegetation Cover Manual.

steps.title: Plan Reapplication
steps.instruction: Schedule reapplication with a minimum interval of six months between treatments.

substeps.instruction: Do not reuse previous perforations due to lignification of vascular tissue.
Install new devices beside previous perforations, maintaining the zig-zag pattern.
